49170: The information disclosure vulnerability allowed the disclosure of user emails through the user_id parameter in the "Manage users" functionality. The emails for user IDs 1, 514755, 514775, and 514764 were disclosed in response to requests made through the application.
170161: The password reset tokens on yelp.com did not expire after the issuance of new tokens. This allowed previously issued, unused tokens to remain usable, even after the user had reset their password.
172933: The issue is that IDN (Internationalized Domain Names) displayed in Unicode in Yelp's messages, about, and talk sections could be exploited to carry out a homograph attack. IDNs that appear similar to legitimate domains could redirect users to spoofed websites. To mitigate this, it was recommended that Yelp display the Punycode version of the IDN URL instead, making it clear to users that the link is not the expected domain.
178831: The sign-up endpoint at https://auto-api.yelp.com/account/create_secure was vulnerable to CSRF attacks. The endpoint processed sign-up requests without checking for valid headers such as cookies, CSRF tokens, or user-agent. This allowed an attacker to create accounts on the victim's behalf by submitting a crafted HTML form.
180538: The X.509 certificate validation failed on international vanity domains. This was not a vulnerability, but rather a TLS/SSL configuration issue with the certificates. Users were unable to access Finnish domain pages without encountering certificate-related errors.
182467: An email spoofing vulnerability allowed users to send emails impersonating Badoo administrators. This vulnerability could potentially lead to phishing attacks or the spread of malicious content.
186554: A stored XSS vulnerability was discovered in the "Address Book" feature of Starbucks' user profile page. The vulnerability was caused by the lack of proper input sanitization on the "Address.FirstName" parameter when a new address was added. This allowed an attacker to inject malicious code that would be executed when a user's profile was viewed.
194351: There was a misconfigured WordPress installation at yelpblog.com that allowed arbitrary PHP files from the wp-includes folder to be downloaded. This provided access to sensitive information about the server's configuration and the WordPress installation.
194721: The Yelp signup/Facebook endpoint allowed an attacker to verify whether a specific email address was registered on Yelp. No rate limiting or validation of CSRF tokens was implemented, enabling the attacker to test a large number of email addresses in a short time.
194832: An authentication bypass vulnerability was discovered on a monitoring server that allowed unauthorised access by connecting a Google account. The issue was similar to a previously reported vulnerability but the fix had not been fully implemented, as a Shopify subdomain could still be accessed by connecting a Google account. This subdomain should have been hidden and protected to only accept Shopify.com Google accounts.
207042: A vulnerability was discovered in the Marketo Forms solution used on a website that allowed contact form data to be stolen. By abusing frame communication techniques and cross-origin requests, an attacker could trigger an cross-site scripting vulnerability. This enabled eavesdropping on contact form submissions and extracting submitted data. The vulnerability relied on the lack of origin checks for messages passed to a cross-origin frame and excessive flexibility in parameters passed to cross-domain requests.
208407: A basic user account was able to be created on the HackerOne Drupal CMS via Google login.
214087: The Yelp website was found to have a clickjacking vulnerability. The vulnerability allowed an attacker to trick users into performing unintended actions, such as bookmarking unwanted businesses, adding events to their profile, and editing their review ratings, without their knowledge or consent. The vulnerability was discovered due to Yelp's use of the "X-Frame-Options" HTTP header, which was not consistently applied across all pages on the site.
217358: A subdomain takeover vulnerability was discovered in info.hacker.one due to a vulnerable parameter in the UnbouncePages application. The attacker was able to claim the subdomain and place new content. Steps to reproduce were provided. The vulnerability impacts HackerOne by allowing the subdomain to be used for phishing and other malicious purposes. Unbounce customers are also impacted since the vulnerability affects all branded domains.
226199: The JIRA integration settings in HackerOne were vulnerable to manipulation through multiple bugs, allowing an attacker to change the victim's settings and connect their own JIRA project to the victim's HackerOne program.
229483: There were validation issues with unicode characters when saving accounts, causing server errors. The permitted characters were not specified.
237357: The website vpn.bitstrips.com was found to be vulnerable to CRLF injection. By injecting a carriage return and line feed character, the attacker was able to make the server issue a set-cookie header with an arbitrary value. The vulnerability was mitigated by stripping out any input containing the %0d%0a URL encoded characters.
240958: The Firefly's verify_access_token() function was found to be vulnerable to timing attacks due to the use of a byte-by-byte comparison of HMAC values, which allowed the termination of the comparison as soon as two characters did not match.
241608: A vulnerability was reported where a user was able to create two accounts with the same email address on Weblate. The user signed up with one email address, added and disconnected that address, then signed up with the same email again. This resulted in two accounts with the same email that could not be logged into, leading to an internal server error.
243616: A vulnerability was found where a previously used password could be set as a new password.
244636: The vulnerability allowed the creation of accounts using the email verification of the original account. The attacker was able to change the email in the confirmation request body to a different email, which resulted in the new account being under the attacker's control and bypassing authorization.
245340: The vulnerability allowed a member of a private leaderboard to change the owner's name by bypassing the access control checks. The member was able to make the changes despite the initial error message indicating they were forbidden from doing so.
246801: A vulnerability was discovered in the Coinbase sign up form that allowed bypassing the CAPTCHA protection. By removing the g-recaptcha-response header when submitting the sign up request, the CAPTCHA could be bypassed, enabling the creation of fake accounts and username enumeration.
247628: A vulnerability was discovered that allowed hackers to exploit the hackbot's automated duplication answers to reveal redacted data through brute force. This vulnerability enabled the identification of redacted text in reports, potentially compromising sensitive information.
262661: An insecure direct object reference (IDOR) vulnerability was discovered in the HackerOne feedback review functionality. This allowed malicious users to create public reviews for any hacker, potentially leading to reputation downgrades.
273630: The configuration file of an internal IRC bot, which included credentials to internal and external services used by Yelp developers, was inadvertently included in a personal public GitHub repository. The repository was taken down and the affected credentials were rotated.
286667: A vulnerability was identified in the password reset functionality that allowed HTML injection. Investigation confirmed it was a self-XSS issue that required a target to copy and paste a payload. The vulnerability occurred on accounts.shopify.com.
